propositions: Detached sweep workers that die between snapshot-write/retire and git commit leave the tracker tree dirty with tracked deletions and untracked snapshot files, causing reconverge to abort on dirty-tree conflict and strand local commits.

The compaction fold performs snapshot-write, retire-rename, and git commit as separate non-atomic steps with no rollback, so a crash or concurrent writer at any boundary corrupts the shared working tree.

An intent journal written before any mutation, combined with ordered fold steps and rollback-on-failure, makes the fold crash-atomic: recovery at the next sweep entry converges a dirty tree to clean with no lost events.

Recovery must discriminate three journal states: snapshot already in HEAD (landed, discard journal only), snapshot uncommitted (abandoned fold, rename sources back and discard snapshot), snapshot gone from disk (superseded or fsck-repaired, discard journal without touching files), and treat transient git faults as indeterminate to avoid misclassifying a landed fold as absent and reverting it.
